events.title: Death of Napoleon Bonaparte
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte, former Emperor of the French, died in exile on the remote island of Saint Helena in the South Atlantic, at the age of 51, after years of declining health.
events.significance: The death of Napoleon closed the chapter on one of history's most influential military and political figures, whose legal reforms (the Napoleonic Code) and conquests reshaped Europe.

events.title: Birth of Karl Marx
events.description: Karl Marx was born in Trier, in the Kingdom of Prussia. He became a philosopher, economist, and revolutionary socialist who co-authored The Communist Manifesto with Friedrich Engels and wrote Das Kapital.
events.significance: Marx's theories on capitalism, class struggle, and historical materialism profoundly influenced political movements, economics, and social sciences throughout the 19th and 20th centuries.

events.title: Alan Shepard Becomes First American in Space
events.description: Astronaut Alan Shepard piloted the Freedom 7 capsule on a suborbital flight of about 15 minutes, launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida, as part of Project Mercury.
events.significance: Shepard's flight was the first American human spaceflight, a key milestone in the Space Race and a step toward the Apollo program and the Moon landings.

events.title: Prague Uprising Begins
events.description: Czech resistance fighters in Prague rose up against the German occupation in the final days of World War II in Europe, as Allied forces closed in and Nazi Germany neared collapse.
events.significance: The uprising helped liberate Prague and demonstrated Czech resistance to Nazi occupation, shortly before Germany's unconditional surrender on May 8, 1945.

events.title: Death of Bobby Sands
events.description: Irish Republican Army member Bobby Sands died on the 66th day of a hunger strike in the Maze Prison in Northern Ireland, protesting the withdrawal of political prisoner status. He had been elected to the UK Parliament weeks earlier.
events.significance: Sands' death drew worldwide attention to the Troubles, galvanized support for Irish republicanism, and boosted Sinn Féin's entry into electoral politics.
